verdict.headline: Iran publishes restrictive Hormuz draft; Dow breaks five-day win streak
verdict.label: SPX 7,710 (−0.18%); Dow 53,885 (−0.85%, 5-day streak ends); SPCX −13.7% at $108.27; WTI $77.29 (+2.8%); Brent $82.49 (+3.8%, near $85 trigger); DDOG −17% on beat; September hike 52%; NFP Friday 8:30 AM ET
verdict.rationale_short: Iran's state media published a restrictive Hormuz draft banning US and Israeli ships and imposing 20% cargo penalties on violators, reversing three sessions of oil relief. WTI jumped 2.8% to $77.29 — $1.71 from the $79 trigger; Brent reached $82.49, $2.51 from the $85 threshold. The 10Y yield rose 6bps to 4.68% on the oil surge, breaking the Dow's five-day win streak (−0.85%). SPCX closed −13.7% at $108.27, confirming the morning's lockup-selling read; the intraday range ($105.11–$115.75) shows institutional buyers below $110. DDOG fell 17% on beat-and-raise fundamentals — the second software name in two sessions to reprice sharply from elevated multiples. Level that changes this: SPX below 7,380 on a Khamenei approval combined with above-consensus NFP.

trade_setups.thesis: 30Y at 5.20% is the sole formal breach; September at 52% is 18 points from the 70% trigger. Friday's NFP (8:30 AM ET; consensus 80–88K; ADP 44K points to downside) is the week's remaining independent variable. Below 80K: September falls below 45%, Kashkari isolated, 30Y has a path toward 5.00%. Above 130K: three dissenters validated, September approaches 70%, and Brent at $82.49 means two regime thresholds could move simultaneously.
trade_setups.entry: Binary event. 5.00% and 5.28% are the formal 30Y clearing levels on either side of the current 5.20%.
trade_setups.invalidation: Khamenei approves the restrictive Hormuz draft before 8:30 AM ET Friday, pushing Brent above $85 and repricing September odds independent of NFP.
trade_setups.horizon: 24 hours through NFP Aug 7; medium term through CPI Aug 13

trade_setups.thesis: Three sessions of oil-deflation momentum reversed on a single draft document. Brent at $82.49 is $2.51 from the $85 trigger; WTI at $77.29 is $1.71 from $79. If Khamenei approves the restrictive draft, both oil triggers breach simultaneously — moving the regime from 1-of-6 to 3-of-6. A Khamenei rejection returns oil toward the $74 territory and re-opens the rate-relief and equity-momentum setup that Tuesday through Wednesday had built.
trade_setups.entry: Brent $85 and WTI $79 are the formal trigger levels. The week's oil decline (11%) has been partially recaptured (3–4%); Khamenei's response resolves the direction.
trade_setups.invalidation: Khamenei rejects the draft or proposes material concessions bringing the framework closer to a full reopening; Brent falls back below $79.
trade_setups.horizon: 24–72 hours for diplomatic resolution; immediate market transmission on any sign

trade_setups.asset: SaaS multiple compression — DDOG as canary
trade_setups.thesis: Datadog fell 17% on Q2 revenue +36% and raised guidance. Figma fell 16.5% on August 5 on a comparable beat-and-raise. The shared variable is not fundamentals but valuation: both traded at 25–30x NTM revenue before the print. DDOG repriced to roughly 20–22x on the day. Whether this signals a structural floor shift for high-growth SaaS multiples will be tested by Snowflake, MongoDB, and other names reporting in the next 2–4 weeks.
trade_setups.entry: Sector-level pattern is forming. The next major SaaS print confirms or refutes it. No specific levels define the setup until one of those names reports.
trade_setups.invalidation: The next major SaaS print beats and holds its pre-earnings multiple; or DDOG recovers above its pre-earnings close within 3 sessions.
trade_setups.horizon: 2–4 weeks through remaining SaaS earnings season

bear_case: Iran's restrictive Hormuz draft, if approved by Khamenei, pushes Brent above $85 and WTI above $79 simultaneously — activating two oil regime thresholds that have not been triggered together this cycle. Friday's NFP landing above 100K in that context removes the labor-softness argument that has kept September hike odds from crossing 70%, and three simultaneous breaches (30Y, Brent, September hike odds) would represent the broadest regime widening since the Iran escalation peaked in June. If SPX closes below 7,380 on that combination, this read no longer holds.
